natsuki.title: Scars and Bets
natsuki.text:
Natsuki takes you up onto the old ramparts at sunset, where the stone is still warm from the afternoon. She sits down on the edge with her legs over the drop, as she used to sit on the wall behind the school.

She pulls up the hem of her shirt to show you a scar below her ribs. It's pale and ragged. She got it in her first week here, from something with too many teeth, before she had learned how to hold a sword.

"Nobody stitched it. I didn't know who to ask." She lets the shirt fall. "Three years, Sam. Cold hostels. Contracts I couldn't read. I got good because the alternative was dying."

You remember the two of you on the curb outside the corner shop, with ice pops melting down your wrists.

"I kept thinking, if Sam walked up right now, he'd do something stupid and we'd somehow both come out breathing." She laughs, roughly, and leans into your shoulder. "Then you finally turn up, and you've inherited a brothel."
ngpp: Even while laughing about summer popsicles back home, she stops half a beat staring at the wall lantern—like a ghost of sharing this same stone bench tugged her sleeve.
"Funny, Sam—I remember every single stupid bike race back home clear as yesterday, yet sitting beside you on THIS town wall feels like we already settled in here once."

"Three years alone wasn't enough to shake me loose, idiot," Natsuki mutters, leaning firmly against your arm despite wiped cycles. "I remember Earth—and every rib in my chest knows this wall bench belongs to us too."

choices.label: Trace the scar gently with your eyes only
choices.res: You don't touch it, but you look, and you let her see you looking. She goes quiet in a way she never was in the old neighborhood, and moves the plaster on her cheek back into place.

choices.label: Admit the dumb thing was on purpose
choices.res: "Totally on purpose," you lie. {N} grins, rubs her plaster, and punches your shoulder, softer than she'd like to admit.

image.comp: showing him a scar on her arm, sitting on a fence, half-smiling

natsuki.title: Incoming
natsuki.text:
You walk into the washroom without knocking. You've been walking into rooms that Natsuki is in since you were six.

She's in the bath. Steam is rising, her chestnut hair is plastered to her forehead, and she's humming something from a cartoon you both watched.

The soap is already in the air.

She doesn't mean anything by it. It's fifteen years of reflex. When you were nine it was a pillow, and when you were twelve it was a shoe. The difference is that she now throws at adventurer speed, and that she is not nine.

Behind the soap, coming toward your face, you can see hers. It's very small and very red. Her other arm has gone across her chest. Her mouth is open, and she's about to call you something she hasn't called you since middle school.

1.title: Soap & Pride
1.text:
You open the washroom door. Natsuki is in the bath with her hair pinned up and her towel thrown over the bench, out of reach.

She goes for the soap out of pure reflex. Her arm comes back. Then she stops, with her cheeks burning, and drops her hand into the water with a huff.

"Quit grinning like that, idiot." She sinks down until the water's at her chin and glares at you over it. "Fine. If you're coming in, make yourself useful. There's a spot between my shoulder blades I haven't been able to reach in three years." She turns her bare back to you, and her ears are scarlet.

choices.label: Kneel beside the tub and scrub her scarred back gently
choices.res: Natsuki stiffens for two stubborn seconds as warm lather works over old sword-calluses and pale scars—before tipping her head back with a sharp breath to catch your mouth in a hot, wet kiss.
choices.fallbackRes: She grumbles the whole time about your terrible massage technique, though she leans squarely back against your knuckles until her ears glow pink.

choices.label: Toss her the bath brush and close the door cleanly
choices.res: "Chicken," she calls after you, though she's laughing against the splash of hot water.

3.title: No More Clothes Between Us
3.text:
Steam rolls out when you open the washroom door.

Natsuki is sitting in the deep wooden tub with one scarred leg hooked over the rim. She's naked and she isn't covering anything. Water is running down her tits and over the hard muscle of her stomach. She looks up at you through her wet fringe with the grin she used to get before a race.

"Took you long enough, Sam." She flicks water at you. "I waited three years in this city. I'm not waiting for you to fold your clothes. Strip off and get in here before it goes cold. I've got plans for you, and they're not gentle."

choices.label: Strip down and climb straight into the tub with her
choices.res: Before you settle waist-deep in the hot water, Natsuki pins your shoulders straight back against the wood and sinks cleanly down onto your cock—riding you hard with damp cheek pressed fiercely to yours.

choices.label: Pin her lightly against the rim and take your time
choices.res: She gasps loudly when your hands slide low under the hot water, gripping your neck tightly while mist hides nothing between you both.

choices.label: Duck
choices.res: You don't duck fast enough. She feels terrible. She laughs anyway, pressing the heel of her hand against her mouth.

choices.label: Take it like a man
choices.res: Direct hit, right between the eyes. "Nice reflexes, hero," she says, sinking up to her nose in the water, amber eyes bright with mischief.

choices.label: Apologize through the door
choices.res: "Knock next time, idiot!" She sounds like she's grinning, and you hear the soap splash into the tub as she forgives you.

image.comp: throwing a bar of soap at adventurer speed from a bath, furious and blushing

natsuki.title: Almost Taiyaki
natsuki.text:
In the evening market the two of you find a stall selling something that is almost taiyaki. The shape is wrong, and it's more a frog than a fish. But the batter is right, and the smell stops you both in the middle of the street.

Natsuki buys ten.

She eats four of them standing up, without saying a word, and she looks happier than you've seen her since she arrived.

Halfway through the fifth she goes quiet. The paper bag crumples slowly in her fist.

"This is going to sound dumb." She isn't looking at you. She's watching a lantern bob away down the street. "Back in high school I just assumed how it would go. I'd end up nagging you over dinner every night. About vegetables, and your posture. I never decided it. I thought it was obvious." She swallows. "Then I walked down one alley, and I spent three years thinking I'd thrown it away. Dumb, right?"

choices.label: Pull her into the empty alley behind the stall and prove she was right
choices.res: You catch her wrist before she walks away, draw her behind the quiet lantern wall away from the crowd, and pin her warm mouth under yours until the paper bag hits the stones.

choices.label: Tell her it isn't dumb
choices.res: "It isn't dumb." Your voice cracks on the second word. She crushes the bag completely and says nothing, but she doesn't stop you from taking her hand.

choices.label: Steal the last taiyaki to break the tension
choices.res: You steal the last one, deadpan. {N} yelps, chases you three stalls down, and laughs herself breathless. Her ears are red when she catches up.

image.comp: eating fish-shaped pastries at a street stall with him, cheeks full, going quiet
image.setting: busy market street, food stalls, afternoon

natsuki.title: Solo Run
natsuki.text:
Natsuki took a dungeon contract without telling anyone. It was a solo run with a deep floor, and the bounty had sat on the guild board for a month because nobody else would touch it.

She's gone for three days. You find out where she went from the bartender.

She comes back through the front door on the third night with her arm in a sling made from her own cloak and a sack of gold over her shoulder. She's grinning through the grime. Her sword is chipped along one edge, and the plaster is gone from her cheek, along with some of the cheek.

"Basically nothing," she announces to the common room. "Two of them. Maybe five. Look at this haul!"

Then she sees your face.

The grin falters. She stands there with the sack still held up. She looks like a kid who has brought home a test with a hundred on it and found that nobody is pleased.
ngpp: When you pull the bandages out before she finishes talking, she blinks sharply—as though she remembers this exact quiet standoff over her bruises.
"Why did you grab the splint out of the bottom cupboard before looking, Sam?" she mutters through gritted teeth, weirdly shaken despite the grin.
She drops straight into the chair before you even scold her, holding out her good arm with rough quiet surrender. "Yeah, yeah—I knew you'd look at me like that, idiot. Patch me up."

choices.label: Yell at her
choices.res: "You don't get to disappear on me twice!" It comes out wrong, too loud, too raw. You don't talk for a while.

choices.label: Patch her up, quietly
choices.res: You don't say anything. You don't have to. She leans her head against yours, breathing out three years of tension.

choices.label: Make her promise
choices.res: "Next time, you come with me," she says, laughing a little. "Deal?" You say deal, and she spits in her palm to shake on it.

image.comp: limping in with a broken arm in a sling and a sack of gold, defiant grin

natsuki.title: Fireworks
natsuki.text:
Natsuki has been up to something with the guild alchemist all week. It has cost her half her savings. Tonight she takes you up onto the east parapet with a sack of salty fried things and makes you sit down and wait.

"August," she says. "The river festival. We went every year. You always got the goldfish game wrong."

Down in the yard, the alchemist lights a fuse and runs.

The first shell splutters up green and lopsided and goes out with a cough. Natsuki swears at it.

The second one climbs. It keeps climbing, well past the rooftops. Then it opens into a wide pink chrysanthemum that lights every slate in Hollowmere and hangs there.

Shutters are opening all over town. Somebody cheers.

She doesn't say anything. Her boots are swinging over the drop, and her shoulder is against yours. In the light of the third shell you can see that her eyes are wet, and that she's smiling.

2.text:
Natsuki has bribed the guild alchemist into firing off homemade shells, like the August festival back home. She sits down on the east parapet close enough that her bare thigh is pressed along yours before the first fuse is lit.

The big pink one goes up and opens over the rooftops. All of Hollowmere turns to look at it.

Natsuki doesn't. She has turned to look at you. The light is moving on her face, and her eyes are bright.

"I planned this for a week," she says. "And now I don't care about the fireworks." Her hand closes in the front of your hoodie. "There's an empty watch-alcove about ten feet behind us. I checked."

choices.label: Hold her hand
choices.res: Her scarred fingers tremble for one second, then lace firmly between yours. Gold light washes over her cheek as the finale bursts, and she never pulls back.

choices.label: Tell her you missed her, all three years
choices.res: She punches your shoulder hard enough to sting, then cries fiercely against your hoodie before laughing while the last rocket drowns everything out.

choices.label: Pull her down into the empty watch-alcove once the smoke clears
choices.res: As the last pink ember fades above the watchtower, Natsuki catches both sides of your collar and pulls you eagerly back into the lantern-lit alcove.

image.comp: watching fireworks from the town wall with him, faces lit up
image.setting: town wall at night, colorful fireworks over rooftops

natsuki.title: Door Kicked In
natsuki.text:
Natsuki kicks your door open at dawn.

She has never been good at knocking, but this is new. The lock splinters under her boot. Cold light comes in behind her. She's red in the face, and her sword is still on her hip. She has plainly been up all night walking the walls and arguing with herself.

"I spent three years here thinking I'd never see you again." She's almost shouting. "And before that I spent a whole life back home pretending we were just kids from the same street. I knew, Sam. I knew when we were fifteen. I was too chicken to say it, so I said 'race you' for ten years."

She takes a breath that shakes.

"I'm not wasting another day. I love you, you idiot. I'm staying, and it's not for the free meals. It never was."

She kicks the door shut behind her. It doesn't latch any more, so she shoves the chair against it.
ngpp: Even kicking the latch splinters feels oddly practiced, like another piece of her remembers losing patience at this exact dawn.
"Don't ask why I feel like I've broken this exact bedroom door already, Sam," she growls flushed to her collarbones as she steps toward your bed.
"Every Earth summer, every wiped cycle in this town—I don't care anymore, Sam," Natsuki breathes fiercely as she unbuckles her sword belt. "You're stuck with me."
natsuki.goLead: Natsuki drops her scabbard onto the chair and shoves you back onto the mattress. She climbs on top of you and straddles your waist, fierce and out of breath and laughing.

choices.label: Say yes
Not yet
choices.res: {N} scowls, then softens. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She repairs the door herself on the way out, badly, and mutters about not being patient.
